title: Twenty-five minutes with GamePlanIQ
intro: A board meeting demo in five acts: a parent, a player, a coach, the league office and the platform. Each step switches to the right person and opens the right screen. Say what is in bold; click what is listed. GamePlanIQ sits on top of Little League Central Registration: register and pay there, import the roster here, run everything else in this app.

acts.title: Act 1 · A parent who never played

steps.title: The parent's home page
say: Every parent lands on what matters today: field status, the next game, a coach's assignment and a report card waiting.
The digest at the top is the same thing a daily email would say.

steps.title: The player's report card
say: The head coach rated ten skills, celebrated three, picked one thing to work on, and the app chose the lessons that teach it for a nine-year-old.
Private to the family, the coach and the league. Never a ranking.

steps.title: Forms without paper
say: The medical form, consents and anything else the league needs are forms built from templates. The parent fills them in once per child on a phone.
Only the coaches, the safety officer and the president can read medical answers.
click: Pick the Player, answer the required questions, Submit

steps.title: A lesson for a scared kid
say: Written for the parent who never played: what to do, what to say, what to avoid, a verified drill video, and a ten-minute practice.
Mark done feeds the player's progress and badges.

steps.title: Game-day duties on the team page
say: Snacks, scorekeeper, dugout parent, per game. Parents claim with one tap; the coach can nudge the whole team.
click: I'll do it on the open snack slot

steps.title: One calendar for the family
say: Games, practices, duties, due dates and deadlines in one file with phone reminders. This is how the league reaches a family that never opens an app.

steps.title: Baseball IQ on the diamond
say: The player's own account: no messages, no leaderboards. Tap where the ball should go; some answers are acceptable, not just right or wrong.
Fifteen lessons and fifty questions, all written for kids.

steps.title: Coaches' Headquarters
say: The Head Coach is a parent with one season of experience. Everything he needs is on one page: practice planner, team tools, game day, certification, tryouts and All-Star ballots.
click: Look at the certification progress and the tryout card

steps.title: Curriculum and evaluations
say: The Comets follow the league's 12-week program. Green weeks were actually run, judged from the practices the head coach finished in the app.
Mid-season he evaluates each player once; it feeds the player's history and next year's team formation.
click: Open Coaches' HQ, then the evaluation form from Forms to complete on Home

steps.title: Game day: lineup and scorebook
say: Before game day the head coach plans every inning on a private sheet (3B through Roster). Only he sees it unless he shares it; Use on game day sends it to the lineup card.
The lineup card checks the league's minimum-play rule, bench innings and pitcher rest before first pitch.
The scorebook is one thumb: run, out, pitch count. Final updates standings and rest days in one tap.
click: Team tools, Game plans tab, open the plan, Use on game day
Scorebook tab, add a run and an out

steps.title: Run a practice from a phone
say: A generated plan becomes a full-screen timer with cues, the drill's setup diagram and the video one tap away. Finish logs it, counts toward the curriculum and sends the home assignment.

steps.title: Tryout scoring board
say: Six stations, one to five, on any phone. Scores from every evaluator roll into the draft board the commissioner runs.
click: Score a player: Save and next

steps.title: Coach certification
say: Six safety and conduct modules with a check at the end. The league sees who is ready to be around players; nobody chases paper.
click: Open the heat and lightning module

steps.title: What needs a decision today
say: The League President sees the attention list first: documents to review, conflicts, a live draft, coaches not yet certified, fields needing a call.
click: Field status: set the Tee Ball Diamond to open

steps.title: Scheduling with conflict detection
say: Drag a game to another day. Field, team, shared-coach and umpire conflicts are flagged; a rainout closes a field and tells every family in one step.

steps.title: Draft board and All-Stars
say: Tryout scores become a snake draft with balance warnings that advise, never block. All-Star nominations, ballots and the tally live here; only selected families are told.

steps.title: End-of-season tournament
say: Round robin, single or double elimination, or pools then a bracket. Games land on every team calendar, and a scorebook final moves the winner on automatically.

steps.title: Bringing the roster over from Central Registration
say: Little League registration runs through Sports Connect today and PlayMetrics next. Export the roster there, choose the source here, and every row is checked and previewed before anything is written.
Divisions that do not draft use Form teams: siblings together, buddy and coach requests honoured, teams balanced by tryout and evaluation ratings.
click: Import CSV, choose PlayMetrics, use the example row
Teams & rosters, Coach pitch, Form teams

steps.title: Payment plans and fundraising
say: Fundraising has its own ledger: every dollar in or out, by campaign and fund, and whether it is in the bank. The banner names anything open, like raffle cash not yet deposited.
Families split fees into monthly installments; the treasurer sees what is overdue on the Finance page and sends reminders in one click.
click: Record a deposit for the raffle cash; the banner turns green

steps.title: Communications and notification rules
say: One announcement reaches the right audience. Every notification follows published rules: topic switches, quiet hours, no duplicates.

steps.title: Public website without code
say: Change the headline, publish, and open the public site. No rosters or player names are ever public.

acts.title: Act 5 · Your league, in fifteen minutes

steps.title: Onboard a league
say: Name, colors, season, divisions, teams and fields. The wizard ends on a working league office ready for the CSV import you just saw.
click: Walk the steps, then Create league

closing: Everything you saw runs on one shared database with role-based permissions enforced on every action, not just hidden in menus.
Little League Central Registration stays the system of record for registration and fees; GamePlanIQ imports the roster and runs everything else.
Payments, email and SMS connect at deployment; the in-app record and the family calendar work today.
